evidence: How the flames ended, from the ACME test sheets (AI reading of the hand-filled scan, not checked by a human; table test_sheets, column out). The sheets tick one of three endings and agree with the table wherever both speak: all 167 tests ticked 'ext. detect' are self_extinguished in the table, and all 78 ticked 'time out' (54) or 'temp. limit' (24) are flow_terminated. The table's flow_terminated therefore covers two different endings. The 24 temperature-limit tests (21088 F1, 21102 C2, 21102 C5, 21106 F1, 21112A1, 21112 C1, 21112 C2, 21153 A4, 21153 C5, 21174 C5, 21196 M2_1, 21209 A1, 21209 B2, 21242 A1, 21270 A3, 21270 A4, 21270 H2, 21277 A1, 21277 H1, 21277 M1, 21277 N1, 21277 P1, 21291 H2, 21291 J1) were cut off early because the burner got too hot: such a flame neither went out by itself nor lasted the scripted time, and whether it would have gone out is not known. The flag burner_over_limit (peak above 450 C) is not the same set: 22 of the 24 carry it (21102 C5 peaked at 449 C; 21270 A4 at 433 C, and its sheet asks whether it timed out instead), and 8 flagged tests ended otherwise (6 time-outs; 21112 A6 and 21174 C6 went out by themselves).
evidence_source: test sheets of PSI-159 (data/transcriptions/PSI-159/, 22 days) against the experiment tables; data/processed/test_sheets
